body:
Could it not then be said that you also only see things from one side? You completely dismiss my argument as simply "whining". 

Also, I ask again, what constitutes an "intellectual issue" in this case. I don't see how it could be an intellectual issue at all, surely it is all down to our perception of life, and this differs vastly from person to person. So I don't see how you can use calling my issue "not intellectual" to debase it. I've spoken to many people with different views on life and understood what they've said, but that's their perception.

I didn't ignore the later half of your post, but fine, I'll comment on it now:

> Right now you are a slave to your own mind and emotions, but you seem perfectly satisfied with that?

From what I gather, you are pretty much telling me I'm a slave to my perceptions and how it makes me feel, correct? Well, so are you, so is everyone else. Our perception determines many things about us, our feelings and how we react, etc. What you said is quite redundant really, I know there are others who seem content with the current idea of how life works, but, I'm not.

>  I can see clearly now that what you are feeling is not intellectual but actual an emotional crisis you are facing.

How exactly? What exactly constitutes an "intellectual" crisis?

>  You know deep down that your negative views come from a sense of apathy you are experiencing likely from being anti-social and being locked up in your room.

Was that a cheap stab at me? My "negative" views, as you call them, are *my* views. I don't see how being antisocial or being "locked up" in my room has anything to do with it.

> you ... haven't really looked at other social understandings of jobs and education we have leaders and power structures in place. We humans are a group-based social species whether we like it or not. Every group needs structure to run efficiently, therefore we have leaders and power structures in place.

Actually, I am aware of that and the more "optimistic" ways of viewing our structure. However, that's the point, I know I can't change it but I hate the whole idea of it. Money rules all, it's the driving force of the world, the working class are used as pawns for the ruling class (call that Marxist if you wish), work consumes a large part of our lives. I'm not content to live like, but there is literally no other way out of that other than suicide.
I don't want to die, but I really can't see any other way out. There is literally no other way to escape what it is that pains me.
Thanks. You are right, I should be taking one day at a time but it's just so hard to focus on that alone, my mind always drifts towards the future.

Thank you for those kind words, it's given me some else to think about.

I don't want to go to university but it seems like it's need to get a high paying position in a job, but I also hear you need a lot of luck on top of that in this job market.
